remit: persistent price, rates and macro trends; reject premature fades
stance_summary: The US hiking cycle is still a live trend, not a completed event. Official SOFR has printed 3.85 after the delivered 25bp hike, US sovereigns are still making higher 1d/1m prints at 99th-percentile 1y levels, and US inflation/labor/activity gauges remain hot. A 99th-percentile 2Y is a discovery signal, not a fade. Keep paying SOFR_2027-03; do not open a duplicate.

trade.structure: outright pay/short CME SR3 March 2027 (SOFR_2027-03 / SR3H7) in implied-rate space; profits if the canonical implied-rate mark rises

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: short/pay SOFR_2027-03 (SR3H7) outright duration: own continuation of the US hiking path through 2027H1, already held as pos-662bff0986be
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: long USDCAD (USD higher): 1m +1.74% and 5d +1.10% USD-up vs CAD, with US labor 75 vs CA labor 38 and CA-US 2Y at -140bp
expression_comparison.rationale: The causal discrepancy is the US policy-path trend, not a CAD-idiosyncratic FX story. SOFR_2027-03 is the liquid SR3 contract that already sits on the book and directly owns additional 2027H1 hike repricing. USDCAD is a consistent but dirtier expression: it mixes BoC energy pass-through, a still-hiking CORRA strip, and a 3m USDCAD drawdown. Rates and spot are both executable from the packet; rates is cleaner, so rates wins.

context_build.causal_mechanism: Hot US inflation and still-firm labor/activity keep the Fed in a hiking regime after the September 16 25bp increase to 3.75-4.00%. Global tightening (BoJ to 1.25%, BoE 6-3 with three hike votes) and an energy shock that is constraining the easing impulse reinforce that the policy-rate trend persists. Premature fades treat the delivered hike and 99th-percentile yields as a peak; continuation requires the front-end implied path to keep repricing higher while those fundamentals hold.
context_build.path_to_current_price: Verified path: US 2Y 4.76 as of 2026-09-18 is +9bp 1d, +13bp 5d, +57bp 1m at the 99.8th 1y / 88th 5y percentile; 5Y 4.86 is +8bp 1d / +51bp 1m at the 99.6th 1y and 5y percentile; 10Y 5.01 is +7bp 1d / +36bp 1m at the 99.6th 1y / 99.9th 5y percentile. US 2s10s has flattened 21bp over 1m to 25bp (0.2nd 1y percentile) because the front end, not term premium, did the work. CME SR3 implied rates: Sep-26 4.00 (+15bp vs overnight 3.85), Dec-26 4.32 (+47bp), Mar-27 4.58 (+73bp), Jun-27 4.72 (+87bp), Sep-27 4.755 (+90.5bp peak) then a gentle decline. Official SOFR jumped from 3.62 on 2026-09-16 to 3.85 on 2026-09-17, matching the delivered hike into cash. The paper mark on SOFR_2027-03 remains 4.58, unchanged versus entry. Inference: the 1m yield surge and 1d post-hike continuation are the same hiking trend, not a reversal. Unknown: post-cutoff SR3 tape after 2026-09-18; NZ rates are unavailable and unused.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known before the decision: futures entered 16 Sep with greater-than-90% odds of a 25bp hike, and August CPI had already kept the tightening bias intact. New since then: the hike was delivered to 3.75-4.00%; official SOFR printed 3.85; August payrolls +162k with positive revisions; August retail sales +1.2% after a downward July revision; ISM Services 55.4 with activity/new orders above 60; BoJ hiked 25bp to a 31-year high; BoE held 3.75% but with three hike votes; the desk thesis is that the energy shock is constraining the global easing impulse. A fully priced hike cannot by itself explain why 2Y/5Y are still printing higher 1d on 18 Sep and why the SR3 strip still slopes up another ~90bp into Sep-27. The new information is confirmation of the hiking regime, not exhaustion of it.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: The SR3 strip assumes roughly 90.5bp of additional tightening from the 3.85 overnight benchmark into a Sep-27 peak of 4.755, with Mar-27 already 73bp above cash at 4.58, then a shallow decline toward 4.545 by Jun-29. That path treats the September hike as the start of a limited remaining cycle that tops out below 4.80 and then eases. Extreme 1y yield percentiles are being read by faders as evidence that the cheapening is complete.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: The priced assumption that is wrong is that 99th-percentile US yields plus a delivered, pre-telegraphed 25bp hike mark the local peak for 2027H1 implied SOFR. With inflation 72, labor 75, activity 69 and consumer 74 still hot, and with global CBs still tightening, Mar-27 at 4.58 is mid-cycle continuation, not a fade level. Housing-pain headlines in Australia and a 99th-percentile screen are not a US reversal signal.
context_build.price_decomposition: Level versus change: the 2Y level 4.76 is historically high on a 1y window, but the economically relevant change is the 1m +57bp front-end selloff that flattened 2s10s by 21bp and 5s10s by 15bp. Tenor: this is a policy-path / 2Y-adjacent move, not a 30Y term-premium event (30Y only +15bp 1m, and -1bp 5d). Strip components: overnight 3.85, near SR3 4.00, Mar-27 4.58, strip peak 4.755. Marginal driver is sequential confirmation of the hiking regime (delivered FOMC, cash SOFR step-up, still-hot gauges, global tightening), not a one-day flow spike. CME positioning is unavailable so flow cannot be shown as the driver.

historical_reference.distribution: US 2Y, 5Y and 10Y all sit at or above the 99th 1y percentile; 2Y is 88th on 5y, 10Y is 99.9th on 5y. US 2s10s at 25bp is the 0.2nd 1y percentile after a 21bp 1m flattening. That distribution is extreme on a 1y window and is the exact screen a mean-reverter wants to fade. It is not, by itself, a completed cycle.
analogs: 2022-2023 Federal Reserve hiking sequence: after each delivered hike and after front-end yields looked statistically extreme, additional hikes continued while inflation and labor stayed firm; fades of the first few 99th-percentile prints were early.
1994 US tightening: a pre-telegraphed first hike did not cap the path; the front end kept cheapening as activity stayed resilient.
historical_reference.regime_differences: Overnight SOFR is already 3.85, not a near-zero start, so remaining hike capacity is smaller than 2022. An energy shock and simultaneous BoJ tightening are present. US Q2 GDP decelerated to +1.5% SAAR and consumer confidence is weak even as August retail and ISM services are strong. Those differences cap how far the analog can be stretched; they do not create a reversal signal in the packet.

trade.thesis: FACT: Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00%; official SOFR is 3.85; SR3H7 / SOFR_2027-03 implied is 4.58, +73bp versus overnight; the strip still peaks at 4.755 in Sep-27; US 2Y 4.76 is +57bp 1m and +9bp 1d; US gauges remain 69-75; BoJ hiked to 1.25% and the desk thesis says the energy shock is constraining global easing. INFERENCE: price, the rate strip, and macro revisions are still aligned with a hiking trend; 99th-percentile yields are what a continuing trend looks like, not a reversal. The clean continuation is to stay short duration in SOFR_2027-03 rather than fade it or migrate to spot. UNKNOWN: live CME positioning, post-18 Sep SR3 ticks, and whether the next CPI/labor print breaks the hot-gauge regime. Book action is HOLD of pos-662bff0986be at 50m; do not OPEN a second SOFR_2027-03.
trade.mispricing: The market is treating a delivered, >90%-priced 25bp hike plus 99th-percentile 1y yields as terminal for 2027H1 SOFR. That underweights the still-hot US gauges, the still-positively-sloped SR3 strip into Sep-27, and the 1d continuation in sovereigns. Fading Mar-27 at 4.58 because later contracts already print 4.72-4.755 is the premature fade: continuation means H7 can still cheapen toward that later peak, and the peak itself can still rise if another hike is delivered.
why_now: The September hike is now in cash (SOFR 3.85) and in the strip, but 1d US 2Y/5Y/10Y prints on 18 Sep are still higher — the trend did not die on announcement.
Independent confirmation from BoJ 1.25% and BoE three hike votes that the global easing impulse is blocked.
Existing short pos-662bff0986be is already the right instrument at an unchanged 4.58 mark; the job is to refuse the fade, not to duplicate the line.

Next labor report that holds unemployment near 4.1% or keeps payrolls firmly positive
Another FOMC 25bp or a higher SR3 peak if the energy shock persists
Global tightening follow-through after BoJ 1.25% and BoE hawkish dissent
principal_risks: The September hike was >90% priced; further strip cheapening may be slower than the 1m 2Y move.
Roll-down on an upward-sloping SR3 strip works against a pay/short if the path is unchanged.
US consumer confidence is weak and Q2 GDP decelerated to +1.5% SAAR; a genuine activity break would end the trend.
Market-state is stale for NZ_rates and CME positioning is missing; a hidden flow unwind cannot be ruled out.
Energy-market shock absorbers and the Saudi workaround can cut both ways for the inflation impulse.
